verdict.rationale: cubic stores its automation configuration (AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, custom agents) in a repo-root `cubic.yaml` that acts as the source of truth, so automations are config-as-code and can be versioned alongside code. Auto-approval also offers a shadow mode for reviewing what the automation would do before switching it live. However, cubic documents no automation version history, change review, or rollback feature of its own; those depend on the user's Git workflow. Missing for 10: first-party version history for automations, a documented review/approval flow for config changes, explicit rollback capability, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations

citations.quote: `cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.

Create a repository named `cubic-config` in your organization and add a `cubic.yaml` file to the root directory. cubic automatically applies these settings to any repository that doesn't have its own configuration.
Start in shadow mode to see which PRs cubic would approve, then switch to live mode
